title: What If You Stood on the Surface of a White Dwarf Star?

scenes.text: What if you stood on a white dwarf? It packs the Sun into Earth's size.
Take Sirius B: about the Sun's mass, but only about 0.88 times Earth's radius.
A teaspoon of white dwarf material would weigh about five and a half tons on Earth. Roughly an elephant.
Surface gravity is at least 100,000 times Earth's. For Sirius B, it's about 380,000.
At that gravity, a 70-kilogram person would weigh over 20,000 tonnes.
And the surface is about 25,000 kelvin, over four times hotter than the Sun's. You'd be crushed and cooked at once.

description:
